advances: Every lattice simplex with the origin as its unique interior lattice point has centered exponential capacity strictly below \(4^r\), even with arbitrary origin barycentric coordinates, lattice index, and facet distances. Thus no simplex can supply a violating seed for the general one-interior-polytope capacity question. The exponential base \(4\) is nevertheless necessary already among simplices. The argument does not settle the general-polytope question or the locked weak Oertel conjecture.

proof:
The barycentric coordinates satisfy \(\sum_{i=0}^r\alpha_i(\mathbf x)=1\); membership in \(P\) is equivalent to \(\alpha_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) for every \(i\), and membership in its interior is equivalent to strict positivity of every coordinate. Since the origin is interior, every \(\beta_i\) is positive. Thus \(k_i(\mathbf I):=\lfloor\alpha_i(\mathbf I)/\beta_i\rfloor\) is a nonnegative integer for \(\mathbf I\in D\).

Suppose \(\mathbf I,\mathbf J\in D\) have the same \(r\) bin coordinates. Write \(\delta_i=\alpha_i(\mathbf I)-\alpha_i(\mathbf J)\). Equality of the bins gives \(|\delta_i|<\beta_i\) for \(1\le i\le r\). Choose \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) with \(\sigma\delta_0\ge0\). Affineness, with constant term \(\alpha_i(\mathbf0)=\beta_i\), gives

\[
\alpha_i\bigl(\sigma(\mathbf I-\mathbf J)\bigr)
=\beta_i+\sigma\delta_i>0\quad(1\le i\le r),
\qquad
\alpha_0\bigl(\sigma(\mathbf I-\mathbf J)\bigr)
=\beta_0+\sigma\delta_0\ge\beta_0>0.
\]

The vector \(\sigma(\mathbf I-\mathbf J)\) is therefore an interior lattice point of \(P\). The hypothesis forces it to equal \(\mathbf0\), proving \(\mathbf I=\mathbf J\) and the injection. This proof uses the entire set \(D\), without any assumption on boundary points or the lattice generated by the vertices.

Since each barycentric function is affine, its gradient is constant and \(\alpha_i(\mathbf x)=\beta_i+\nabla\alpha_i\cdot\mathbf x\). For the vector \(\boldsymbol\theta\) in the statement, the injection gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}e^{\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf I}
&=2^r\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}2^{-\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i(\mathbf I)/\beta_i}\\
&\le2^r\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}2^{-\sum_{i=1}^r k_i(\mathbf I)}\\
&<2^r\sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^r}2^{-\sum_{i=1}^r k_i}
=2^r\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}2^{-k}\right)^r
=4^r.
\end{aligned}
\]

The strict inequality holds because \(D\) is finite, its bin map is injective, and every term of the infinite geometric series is positive. Taking the infimum over all real tilts proves the first assertion. No integrality of the barycentric functions or of their gradients has been used.

For the calibration, the complete real description is \(Q_r=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^r:x_i\ge-1\text{ for every }i,\ \sum_{i=1}^r x_i\le1\}\). Its vertices are \(-\mathbf1\) and \(-\mathbf1+(r+1)\mathbf e_i\), so it is a full-dimensional lattice simplex. An interior lattice point has every coordinate nonnegative and has coordinate sum strictly below \(1\). It must therefore be \(\mathbf0\), which itself satisfies all the inequalities strictly.

For every lattice point \(\mathbf I\in Q_r\), set \(m_i=I_i+1\) for \(1\le i\le r\) and \(m_0=r+1-\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\). These formulas give a bijection from the complete lattice support onto the nonnegative integer tuples \((m_0,\ldots,m_r)\) with sum \(r+1\). The inverse is \(I_i=m_i-1\), so no support points are omitted. Placing \(r\) separators among \(r+1\) identical units counts these tuples as \(\binom{2r+1}{r}\). Their uniform law is invariant under every permutation of the \(r+1\) coordinates. Each \(m_i\) consequently has expectation \(1\), and each \(I_i\) has expectation \(0\).

Writing \(N=\binom{2r+1}{r}\), this mean identity and \(e^t\ge1+t\) yield \(\sum_{\mathbf I\in Q_r\cap\mathbb Z^r}e^{\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf I}\ge N+\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\sum_{\mathbf I\in Q_r\cap\mathbb Z^r}\mathbf I=N\) for every \(\boldsymbol\theta\). Equality at \(\boldsymbol\theta=\mathbf0\) proves \(B(Q_r)=N\).

The two central coefficients of the binomial expansion of \((1+1)^{2r+1}\) are its largest coefficients, as follows from the adjacent-coefficient ratio \(\binom{2r+1}{j+1}/\binom{2r+1}{j}=(2r+1-j)/(j+1)\). Hence \(N\ge2^{2r+1}/(2r+2)=4^r/(r+1)\). The already proved strict upper bound applies to \(Q_r\). Taking \(r\)-th roots, using \((r+1)^{1/r}\to1\), proves the limit and the impossibility of a smaller uniform exponential base.
statement:
Let \(r\ge1\), and let \(P\subset\mathbb R^r\) be a full-dimensional lattice simplex satisfying \(\operatorname{int}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^r=\{\mathbf0\}\). Retain its complete lattice support \(D=P\cap\mathbb Z^r\), including every boundary lattice point, and define its unweighted exponential capacity at the target \(\mathbf0\) by \(B(P)=\inf_{\boldsymbol\theta\in\mathbb R^r}\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\exp(\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf I)\). Then \(B(P)<4^r\).

More precisely, let \(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_r\) be the affine barycentric coordinate functions of \(P\), and put \(\beta_i=\alpha_i(\mathbf0)>0\). After omitting any one coordinate and labelling it \(0\), the map \(\mathbf I\mapsto(\lfloor\alpha_i(\mathbf I)/\beta_i\rfloor)_{i=1}^r\) is injective on \(D\). The explicit real vector \(\boldsymbol\theta=-(\log2)\sum_{i=1}^r\nabla\alpha_i/\beta_i\) satisfies \(\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}\exp(\boldsymbol\theta\cdot\mathbf I)<4^r\).

For the calibration, let \(\Delta_r=\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf0,\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_r\}\), let \(\mathbf1\) be the all-ones vector, and write \(Q_r=(r+1)\Delta_r-\mathbf1\). The symbol \(Q_r\) denotes this calibration simplex. Its unique interior lattice point is \(\mathbf0\), its uniform law on the complete lattice support has mean \(\mathbf0\), and

\[
B(Q_r)=\binom{2r+1}{r},
\qquad
\frac{4^r}{r+1}\le B(Q_r)<4^r,
\qquad
\lim_{r\to\infty}B(Q_r)^{1/r}=4.
\]

Consequently no constant \(b<4\) can satisfy \(B(P)\le b^r\) for every such lattice simplex in every dimension. All logarithms are natural.
